name: Wenxin Keli (Chinese herbal medicine)
short: Atrial fibrillation meta-analysis: safety still uncertain. 4-week placebo trial, 1200 people with extra heartbeats: no severe side effects from the formula. Reviews: no excess adverse effects.
text: A 2013 meta-analysis of 14 randomized trials of Wenxin Keli, alone or added to Western medicines, in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation rated trial quality as generally low; seven trials reported adverse events, and the authors judged the safety of Wenxin Keli still uncertain. In a 4-week multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 1200 people in China with frequent premature ventricular contractions (extra heartbeats) and no structural heart disease, no severe adverse effects attributable to Wenxin Keli were reported; the abstract does not list milder events. A 2026 overview of 11 systematic reviews in premature ventricular beats found no significant difference in adverse effects when Wenxin Keli was added to conventional Western medicines, but rated most of the evidence low or very low quality. When combined with amiodarone in heart failure with ventricular arrhythmia, a meta-analysis of 13 trials (randomized or quasi-randomized trials were eligible; risk of bias was high in 3 and unclear in 10; 6 reported adverse events) found no obvious difference in reported adverse events compared with amiodarone alone; the abstracts do not list the formula's herbs, and no other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
